Best way to learn proper typing for someone with poor typing habits?
I never learned how to type the 'correct' way, I still do it the 'wrong' way, but I've gotten much better just due to persistence and experience.

Practice practice practice. Open up a book and transcribe it with proper punctuation without looking at the screen or the keyboard. The best way that I'm aware of to get better at typing is just typing a lot.

I'm sure there are some online classes, but really just typing and challenging yourself with speed tests and the like online will improve skills. If one wants to better typing what they are reading without looking at their hands, you can make a cover so you can't see your hands typing or the keyboard (even a cloth would work if it isn't obnoxious). Another fun thing to do is to blindfold yourself and to try typing what someone says.

If you want to be a great typist by standards of a career, perhaps pick up a typing education book with the ins and outs of hand positions and such.
typingclub.com is how I got better at it.

There are many many classes online, I think this one looks good. I do proper home row typing at 100+ wpm and all I did was follow (a different) class (like 10 years ago, but they should all be relatively the same). It's only important to learn proper hand placement and to stop looking at the keyboard, but it will also give good word lists to practice with (e.g. words that can all be typed on the home row like slash dad gall and fad.)

home row, home row, home row, home row, home row - whenever you put your hands on a keyboard left index on f and right index on j. Don't look at the keyboard even when you have to guess. After a while it becomes muscle memory. You will quickly be able to notice the little indexing bumps on f and j so you don't have to look every-time you adjust your hands.

If you need it at first put a keyboard layout on the screen but don't look at your hands!
